Title: Iohannis Cassiani Opera, Pars I: Prolegomena, Institutionum libri XII, Contra Nestorium libri VII, Indices (John Cassian, Collected Works)
Creator: John Cassian (c. 360 - c. 435) -- Latin text, ed. Michael Petschenig
Publisher: Corpus Scriptorum Ecclesiasticorum Latinorum (CSEL), vol. XVII (Prague/Vienna/Leipzig: F. Tempsky / G. Freytag)
Publication Date: 1888
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: 1888 publication, long out of US copyright (>95 years); archive.org item confirmed Public Domain Mark 1.0.
Source: archive.org item `bub_gb_-QVLAAAAYAAJ` (Google-digitized library copy), OCR text (DjVuTXT), downloaded directly 2026-09-13.
Language: lat
Provenance note: this header was prepended by the build thread; the raw OCR carried none. Not re-transcribed or corrected; OCR noise typical of Latin critical editions with apparatus criticus (broken diacritics, u/v conflation, garbled page/line numbers, Google Books "Digitized by Google" scan-artifact lines) is preserved as scanned.
Content note: full Pars I of Petschenig's edition as scanned -- Prolegomena (manuscript tradition), the complete Institutionum libri XII (all twelve books of the Institutes, including Book VI "De spiritu fornicationis," the book Gibson's NPNF II.11 translation (already vendored, npnf211) omits entirely on Victorian-era grounds -- confirmed present in this file at the "Incipit de spiritu fornicationis... liber sextus" heading, with a full run of chapter capitula and body text following, ending where "Incipit de spiritu filargyriae... liber septimus" begins), Contra Nestorium libri VII (De Incarnatione -- Cassian's anti-Nestorian treatise, already corpus-mapped to this world via npnf211/gal-src-03, but that vendored copy is also NPNF's English translation; this is the Latin critical text of the same work), and the volume's own Indices. No public-domain English translation of Institutes Book VI exists in this project's library. Vendored for Gallic Monastic-Ascetic Christianity (era 2, c. 360-450): closes the specific gap gallic.core.gallic's own .thinness field names ("Three whole texts on the sexual body and its discipline (Conferences XII and XXII, and the Institutes' sixth book) were removed by a nineteenth-century translator from the one edition this build can read -- an edition's absence, not our own silence"). Latin only; second-witness rule applies (Latin original, not this world's evidence-language) -- no translation effort has been made, and no WRS record cites this file as of vendoring. Research handoff from a scheduled source-research routine (2026-09-13), independently re-verified by this build thread (direct download + grep for "LIBER SEXTVS"/"fornicationis" confirming the book's actual presence, not merely its title) before vendoring.

LIBER  QUARTUS. 

I.  Consumniatis  libellis  tribus  quasi  fidelissimis  atque  opu- 
lentissimis  testibus,  utpote  quoruni  ueritas  non  humanis  tantum. 
sed  etiam  diuinis  testimoniis  loeupletata  est,  sufficere  quideni 
nobis  ad  causae  probationem  per  diuinam  auotoritatem  abunde 
poterant,  cum  ipsa  per  se  utique  catisao  suae  auctoritas  diuina 
suffieiat.  scd  tamen  quia  plena  est  his  testimouiis  sacrorum 
uoluminum  series,  ubi  tot  testes  sunt  quot  sententiae,  immo 
ubi  ipsa  scriptura  sacra  quasi  unum  quodammodo  diuiui  oris 
est  testimonium,  aeeumnlanda  quaedam  adhue  putauimus  non 
pro  necessitate  approbationis,  sed  pro  faeultate  rerum  et  eopia, 
ut,  quidquid  neccssarium  non  esset  defensioni,  totum  profieeret 

2  oruatui.  ergo  quia  superioribus  libris  dominum  lesum  Christuni 
non  propheticis  tantum  atque  apostolicis,  sed  etiam  euangelicis 
atque  angelieis  testimoniis,  cum  in  carne  atque  in  terra  esset, 
deum  probauimus,  nunc  eum  qui  in  carne  uatus  est  etiam  ante 
carnis  suseeptionem  deum  semper  fuisse  monstremus,  ut  iutel- 
legas  consentientibus  et  quasi  eonclamantibus  sibi  diuinorum 
uoluminum  testimoniis  eundem  te  post  natiuitatem  corpoream 
et  hominem  debere  oredere  et  deum,  quem  anto  natiuitatem 
oorpoream  tantum  doum,  et  quem  post  editionem  uirginis  in 
corporo  doum,  eundom  anto  partum  uirginis  uerbum  deum. 

3  disoe  orgo  primum  ab  apostolo  totius  mundi  magistro  oum  qui
